bib.title: J1: Incentivizing Thinking in LLM-as-a-Judge via Reinforcement Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "J1: Incentivizing Thinking in LLM-as-a-Judge via Reinforcement Learning", Chenxi Whitehouse, Tianlu Wang, Ping Yu, Xian Li, Jason Weston, Ilia Kulikov, Swarnadeep Saha (FAIR at Meta). No venue is printed on the PDF; the only stamp is "arXiv:2505.10320v3 [cs.CL] 13 Oct 2025", so treat it as a preprint, 2025.

File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/whitehouse-2025-j1.pdf

COVERAGE: 24 of 24 pages, 78,633 of 78,633 chars. Main text p1-10, references p11-14 (skimmed for origins), appendices A-D p15-24 read in full, including Tables 5-13. Figures 1-5 are images: I read their captions and axis labels only, not the plotted values.

CLAIMS

- claim: The best model, a 32B multitask judge, reaches 76.8 overall accuracy on PPE Correctness, +10.3 over its base model.
  number: 76.8 (base Qwen3-32B 66.5)
  setup: PPE Correctness, 12.7K pairs (MMLU-Pro, MATH, GPQA, MBPP-Plus, IFEval), pairwise, accuracy over random response order, trained on 22K synthetic pairs.
  quote: "J1 also improves upon the base Qwen3-32B model, a strong thinking-LLM, by a large10.3%(66.5→76.8)."
  where: p6 (Table 1 on p5)

- claim: Online RL beats offline DPO on the same 22K pairs, and beats a judge trained on far more data.
  number: EvalPlanner-Llama-70B 70.2, DeepSeek-GRM-27B 59.8 (237K pairs), J1-Llama-70B 72.9
  setup: PPE Correctness, same as above. The DeepSeek and scalar-RM rows are copied from other papers, not re-run.
  quote: "outperforms both EvalPlanner (Saha et al., 2025) by 6.8% (70.2→76.6 ), and DeepSeek-GRM-27B (Liu et al., 2025b) by 17% (59.8→76.8 )"
  where: p6. The "76.6" is the paper's own typo; Table 1 says 76.8.

- claim: Across five benchmarks the 32B judge averages above o1-mini, o3 and DeepSeek-R1, but wins only three of the five individually.
  number: Overall 80.8 vs o1-mini 72.7, o3 77.4, R1-671B 78.4. It loses PPE (71.8 vs 72.1 and 72.3) and JudgeBench (71.4 vs o3 75.7).
  setup: PPE, RewardBench (3K), RM-Bench (4K), JudgeBench (350 pairs, GPT-4o subset), FollowBenchEval (205 pairs). The last two use position-consistent accuracy.
  quote: "J1-Qwen-32B-MultiTask80.8 +3.5 71.8 +5.1 93.6 +2.7 90.3 +2.2 71.4 +0.6 77.1 +7.1"
  where: p6, Table 2

- claim: Trained pairwise judges still flip their verdict when the answer order is swapped, in 14.5-21.9% of cases.
  number: J1-Llama-70B pairwise: 72.9 / 72.3 per-order accuracy, 61.2 consistent accuracy, 21.9 flips. Pointwise: 65.0 consistent, 13.7 ties.
  setup: PPE Correctness, greedy decoding.
  quote: "J1-Llama-70BPairwise 72.9 72.3 61.2 21.9"
  where: p6, Table 3

- claim: The untrained 8B base judge flips on 44.1% of pairs; both-order training data barely helps, and the consistency reward is what cuts flips.
  number: flips 44.1 (base), 36.7 (single-order data), 36.8 (both-order data), 28.7 (consistency reward); consistent accuracy 30.2, 38.3, 39.1, 43.9
  setup: Llama-3.1-8B, PPE Correctness.
  quote: "Verdict Consistency Reward 58.4 58.2 43.9 28.7 52.3 64.6 45.4 26.0"
  where: p24, Table 8

- claim: Pointwise wins under the strict position-consistent metric, pairwise wins under random ordering, and the multitask model beats both.
  number: none beyond Table 3
  setup: PPE Correctness.
  quote: "pairwise judges can be position-inconsistent, pointwise judges on the other hand are consistent but lack the context of reference candidates to ground their evaluations on and hence are more prone to ties."
  where: p7-8

- claim: Sampling 32 judgments helps a pointwise judge a lot and a pairwise judge very little.
  number: pointwise mean-score@32: 65.0 to 74.8; pairwise majority vote@32: 72.9 to 73.7
  setup: J1-Llama-70B, PPE Correctness, temperature 1, top-p 0.95.
  quote: "J1-Llama-70B (Mean-Score@32)74.8 81.2 87.6 67.3 81.9 70.8"
  where: p24, Tables 12-13

- claim: On RewardBench the model tops the listed generative judges by a small margin.
  number: 93.6 vs 93.5 (TextEval-Llama3.1-70B), 93.3 (Skywork-Critic-70B), GPT-4o 86.7, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 84.2
  setup: RewardBench overall; most rows come from the leaderboard. RewardBench was also the model-selection set.
  quote: "Model selection is based on overall accuracy on RewardBench."
  where: p5; Table 6 on p23

- claim: Cost: thoughts settle around 500 tokens for pairwise and 300-400 for pointwise; training took 8 to 64 A100s.
  number: as stated
  setup: J1-Llama-8B training curves; GRPO, 5 rollouts per prompt, batch 512, learning rate 1e-6.
  quote: "We use 8×A100 to train J1-Llama-8B, 32×A100 GPUs for J1-Qwen-32B and 64×A100 GPUs for J1-Llama-70B."
  where: p9, p22

- claim: A generative judge beats a Bradley-Terry scalar reward model on the same base and data on four of five benchmarks.
  number: overall 69.2 vs 66.6
  setup: Llama-3.1-8B. See PROBLEMS: this table's numbers disagree with Table 2.
  quote: "J1-Llama-8B(generative) 69.2 59.8 85.7 73.4 58.5 68.8"
  where: p24, Table 11

- claim: Reward design: positive-only reward is best; negative or format rewards slightly hurt; the plan-and-execute seed prompt performs about the same.
  number: overall 61.8 vs 60.4 (negative) vs 61.0 (format) vs 62.1 (plan and execute)
  setup: Pairwise J1-Llama-8B.
  quote: "+ Negative Reward for Incorrect Verdict 60.4 59.6 85.4 44.9 70.8 42.0"
  where: p8, Table 4

LIMITS
- There is no limitations section and the authors concede nothing explicitly.
- No agreement with human raters (kappa, correlation) is reported, only accuracy against benchmark labels. Only PPE Preference (10.2K) is human-preference data, and it is never broken out from the combined PPE number.
- Only position bias is measured. Length and name bias are addressed in the prompt only, with no measurement.
- No inference cost, latency or price comparison against API judges. No model or code release is stated; the reproducibility statement covers prompts and hyperparameters.
- Pointwise scores are trained only to rank pairs, so absolute score calibration is untested.
- No rubric-based or reference-based grading, no multi-turn, no listwise ranking beyond pairs.
- JudgeBench (350) and FollowBenchEval (205) are small, with no confidence intervals. The only uncertainty reported is p < 0.0001 on PPE Correctness and ±0.1 over 8 seeds.
- Checkpoint selection on RewardBench makes the 0.1-point lead there weak evidence.
- Dated: the baselines are o1-mini, o3, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

BUILDS ON
- GRPO: Shao et al., 2024. RL for reasoning: DeepSeek-R1, Guo et al., 2025a.
- Synthetic preference pairs and noisy-instruction rejects: Wang et al., 2024d (Self-Taught Evaluators); Wang et al., 2024a.
- Same data and DPO baseline: EvalPlanner, Saha et al., 2025.
- Position bias: Wang et al., 2024c; Chen et al., 2024.
- Judge prompting: Zheng et al., 2023. Training framework verl: Sheng et al., 2024.
- Benchmarks: Frick et al., 2025; Lambert et al., 2025; Tan et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2025a.

CODE: none. The verbatim pairwise seed prompt is Figure 9 (p17), including: "Avoid any position biases and ensure that the order in which the responses were presented does not influence your decision. Do not allow the length of the responses to influence your evaluation. Do not favor certain names of the assistants."

FIGURES: one candidate, Figure 2, p3: "Reinforcement Learning recipes for training J1 models...". It shows in one diagram how both orderings go in a batch and how the correctness and consistency rewards and the pointwise distant supervision fit together. The alternative is Figure 4 (p7), test-time scaling against N samples.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is clean apart from dropped spaces in headings and table cells that run together (for example "44.769.158.3" in the Skywork row).
- Internal inconsistencies in the paper itself:
  - "70.2→76.6" in the text against 76.8 in Table 1.
  - The same 8B verdict row has Overall 61.8 in Table 4, 61.9 in Table 2 and 63.9 in Tables 7 and 10.
  - Table 11's J1-Llama-8B row gives JudgeBench 73.4 and RM-Bench 58.5, against 42.0 and 73.4 in Table 2. Do not cite Table 11's per-benchmark numbers.
  - Table 4 labels the default prompt "Figure 10" and plan-and-execute "Figure 9", which is reversed.
  - p10 says the concurrent RL judges are compared "in Tables 1 and Table 4"; they are actually in Table 6, and JudgeLRM appears in no table.
- Embedded instructions: the appendix prompt templates (Figures 9-14) and the Table 5 example contain imperative text addressed to a judge model. I treated it as paper content and did not act on it.
